clue.text: Bar for some ladies to patronise

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pub bar reserved for some women customers to frequent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes part of 'ladies to patronise'. ESTOP is a legal term: a bar preventing someone from asserting a claim.
explanation.definitionFit: In law an estoppel or estop is an impediment, so the legal verb and noun sense of barring fits.

clue.text: Winestore is a short distance in a car

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the vehicle word that follows

parts.note: car taken as written
an ell is an old measure of length, about 45 inches

explanation.surface: A wine merchant's premises described as only a short drive away.
explanation.walkthrough: An ELL is an old cloth measure, a short distance; it goes inside CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine is traditionally kept below ground in a basement store.

clue.text: Cessation of work means reduction in pay

explanation.surface: A strike that leads to docked wages.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike is a halt to work, and a deduction taken from wages is also called this.

clue.text: Publicise wine where it's duty free

parts.note: to air an opinion is to make it public
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: Advertise a wine sold tax-free.
explanation.definitionFit: Travellers buy tax-free goods in the departure lounge before a flight.

clue.text: Looking round for a letter?

explanation.surface: Seeking out a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Round in shape is one sense; a printed notice sent to many people is the other.

clue.text: Final defeat in test match

parts.note: to check something is to test it
a mate is one of a pair, a match

explanation.surface: Losing the decisive test match at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: A test match is an international cricket fixture, but here 'test' and 'match' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the game ends when the king is trapped, the ultimate loss.

clue.text: Confirm when definite

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
certain means sure or definite

explanation.surface: Verify something once it is sure.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish a fact for sure is to verify it.

clue.text: Spectacle in which a bull appears?

definitions.text: Spectacle in which a bull appears?

parts.words: Spectacle in which a bull appears?
parts.note: suggests a bullfight show, but a rifle's aiming device frames the bull's-eye of a target

explanation.surface: A show featuring a bull, such as a bullfight.
explanation.walkthrough: The bull is the centre of a target, which a marksman lines up through the aiming device on the gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is something seen, and a gun's aiming device lines up the target.

clue.text: An uplifting tune for singing

parts.note: an gives the letter A

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifting turns the word for tune upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: an air is a melody

explanation.surface: A cheering melody to sing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' reverses AIR to RIA in this down clue; A goes before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An operatic solo song is a melody written to be sung.

clue.text: Sweet sort of lady giving children guidance

definitions.text: sort of lady giving children guidance

explanation.surface: A kind woman who helps children.
explanation.walkthrough: A British lollipop lady is a school crossing patrol, carrying a round sign on a pole that resembles a sweet on a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiled sweet on a stick is one sense; a school crossing patrol is named after the round sign she carries.

clue.text: Gold backing used by firms for ornamental decoration

indicators.note: backing means the word for gold is read from the end

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
two firms, each CO, the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Gold leaf funded by companies for decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns OR into RO; 'firms' is plural, so two COs follow.
explanation.definitionFit: An elaborate eighteenth-century style full of scrolls and shells.

clue.text: Long period return to a district

indicators.note: return means the word for long period is turned round

parts.note: an era is a long span of time

explanation.surface: Going back to a neighbourhood after many years away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns ERA into ARE, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A region or zone of a town.

clue.text: Bring up a 50-amp light for the back of the car

definitions.text: light for the back of the car

parts.note: to rear children is to bring them up
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fit a fifty-amp bulb at the tail of the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: The red tail light on a vehicle.

clue.text: It comes from Mecca, this religious instruction

indicators.note: the answer is made out of the letters of the following words, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Religious teaching originating in the holy city of Islam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It comes from' signals the letters of MECCA THIS are rearranged; Mecca is Islamic, but the result is Christian teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: A question-and-answer summary of Christian doctrine taught to converts.

clue.text: Agreed everything was bound to come out

indicators.note: was, with bound, pictures the word for everything held inside

parts.note: tied means bound
all means everything

explanation.surface: Everyone accepted it was bound to come out.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL is bound inside TIED. Accounts are said to tally when they agree, or come out right.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures that correspond or match are said to do this.

clue.text: Ignore the French welcome abroad

parts.note: le is French for the
ave is a Latin greeting, hail
out means away from home, abroad

explanation.surface: Snub a French greeting while overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit or exclude something is to disregard it.

clue.text: Conceal a confidential note

parts.note: secret means confidential
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Hide a private memo.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide something away, as an animal hides food.

clue.text: Late rising around here-that's heavenly!

indicators.note: around means the reversed word wraps the next one
in a down clue rising means the word late reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation about something sublime appearing in a late sunrise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns LATE into ETAL, and 'around' puts it round HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Light, airy and celestial, as if from the sky above.

clue.text: Utterly pompous

parts.note: utterly looks like completely but means in what one utters, so speech that is grand and inflated

explanation.definitionFit: Describes a booming, bombastic speaking voice or style.

clue.text: Can't have venison without a bottle of wine

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the deer word surrounds

parts.note: venison is deer meat
cant with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: No venison can be eaten without a bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: DEER goes round CANT, ignoring the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass vessel into which wine is poured to let sediment settle.

clue.text: Bound to sound like a current variation

indicators.note: to sound like says the answer is heard as another word

parts.note: the sea's flow that rises and falls is a tide

explanation.surface: Sure to resemble a modern version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' suggests modern, but it is a flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Tied up means fastened or bound.

clue.text: Robin the poet!

explanation.surface: An exclamation identifying a bird as a versifier.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin Hood is the English outlaw; Thomas Hood was a Victorian poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin the outlaw of Sherwood is one sense; Thomas, the nineteenth-century English writer of verse, is the other.

clue.text: Dress I put on about spring

indicators.note: about means the word on goes round the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
rig means dress, as in rig out
taken as written

explanation.surface: Putting on clothes around springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: RIG and I go inside ON. 'spring' is a source, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: A source or wellspring is where something begins.

clue.text: Mention a price

explanation.surface: Name a cost.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite or refer to is one sense; an estimated cost given for a job is the other.

clue.text: It's said to produce a smile

definitions.text: It's said to produce a smile

parts.words: It's said to produce a smile
parts.note: the word photographers ask people to say so their mouths form a grin

explanation.definitionFit: A dairy food whose name, spoken for the camera, stretches the lips into a grin.

clue.text: Public transport stops here when time runs out

explanation.surface: Buses halt here at the end of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: The final stop of a bus or train route is one sense; an end point or deadline in time is the other.

clue.text: It may be forced to obtain a decision

definitions.text: It may be forced to obtain a decision

parts.words: It may be forced to obtain a decision
parts.note: alludes to the idiom about pressing a disputed matter to a resolution

explanation.definitionFit: A disputed point or topic, which one may force to settle it.

clue.text: Never satisfied, Titania's changed direction

indicators.note: changed says the letters of the fairy queen's name are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its S counted
E for east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: The fairy queen has altered course and is still never content.
explanation.walkthrough: Titania is the fairy queen in A Midsummer Night's Dream. 'changed' rearranges TITANIAS; E for east follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Greedy and impossible to fill or appease.
